steps.title: Import required Node.js modules
steps.instruction: Import the http, crypto, and url modules from Node.js using the require() syntax.
steps.hint: Use require('module_name') for each module. These are built-in Node.js modules, so no npm installation is needed.
steps.expectedOutcome: The http, crypto, and url modules are imported and ready to use for building the webhook receiver.
successCriteria: The http, crypto, and url modules are imported using require().
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported the core Node.js modules needed for your webhook receiver.
steps.feedbackPartial: You imported some modules, but make sure to import all three: http, crypto, and url.
steps.feedbackWrong: The required modules are not imported correctly. Use require() to import http, crypto, and url.

steps.title: Create the main server function
steps.instruction: Create a function named 'createWebhookServer' that will handle setting up the HTTP server. The function should take no parameters and return nothing for now.
steps.hint: Define a function using either 'function createWebhookServer()' or 'const createWebhookServer = () =>' syntax.
steps.seedCode:
// Import the required modules here

// Create the main server function here
steps.expectedOutcome: A function named 'createWebhookServer' is defined in your code.
successCriteria: The 'createWebhookServer' function is properly defined with a function body.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the main server function. This will be the foundation for your webhook receiver.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the function is named exactly 'createWebhookServer' and has a function body.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function wasn't created correctly. Please create a function named 'createWebhookServer' that will handle server setup.

steps.title: Initialize server configuration
steps.instruction: Inside your server function, define two constants: one for the port number (e.g., 3000) and another for your webhook secret (e.g., 'your-webhook-secret').
steps.hint: Use the const keyword to declare both variables. The port should be a number, and the secret should be a string.
steps.expectedOutcome: Your server function now contains two constant declarations for configuration values.
successCriteria: The function contains a PORT constant with a numeric value and a WEBHOOK_SECRET constant with a string value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully set up the basic configuration for your webhook server.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've defined both constants: one for the port and one for the secret.
steps.feedbackWrong: The configuration constants aren't defined correctly. Check that you've declared both PORT and WEBHOOK_SECRET inside the function.

steps.title: Create request body parsing helper
steps.instruction: Inside the webhookReceiver function, create a helper function named parseRequestBody that takes a request object as a parameter and returns a Promise that resolves with the parsed request body.
steps.hint: You'll need to collect data chunks from the request stream and concatenate them into a complete string, then parse it as JSON.
steps.expectedOutcome: A parseRequestBody function is created inside webhookReceiver that properly handles request streams and returns a Promise with the parsed JSON body.
successCriteria: The parseRequestBody function is defined inside webhookReceiver, takes a request parameter, returns a Promise, collects data chunks, and parses JSON.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created a proper request body parsing helper that handles the streaming nature of HTTP requests.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your function returns a Promise and properly handles the 'data', 'end', and 'error' events on the request object.
steps.feedbackWrong: The parsing helper isn't quite right. Remember you need to handle the request as a stream and parse the complete body as JSON.

steps.title: Create signature verification function
steps.instruction: Inside the webhookReceiver function, create a function named verifySignature that takes payload and signature as parameters.
steps.hint: Define a function using either function declaration or arrow function syntax. The function should have two parameters: payload and signature.
steps.expectedOutcome: The webhookReceiver function now contains a verifySignature function with payload and signature parameters.
successCriteria: A verifySignature function is defined inside webhookReceiver with two parameters: payload and signature.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the signature verification function structure. Next we'll implement the actual HMAC verification logic.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've defined a function named verifySignature with two parameters (payload and signature) inside the webhookReceiver function.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. Create a function called verifySignature that takes payload and signature as parameters, placed inside the webhookReceiver function.

steps.title: Set up request handler logic
steps.instruction: Inside the webhookReceiver function, create a function named handleRequest that takes request and response parameters.
steps.hint: Define a function that will process incoming HTTP requests. It should accept both request and response objects as parameters.
steps.expectedOutcome: A handleRequest function is defined inside webhookReceiver, ready to process incoming webhook requests.
successCriteria: The handleRequest function is created with request and response parameters.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the request handler function. This will be the core logic for processing webhook requests.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've defined a function named handleRequest that takes both request and response parameters.
steps.feedbackWrong: The request handler function isn't properly defined. Create a function named handleRequest inside webhookReceiver that accepts request and response parameters.

steps.title: Parse incoming webhook data
steps.instruction: Inside the request handler logic, implement the parsing of the JSON payload from the request body.
steps.hint: Use JSON.parse() on the raw body string to convert it into a JavaScript object.
steps.expectedOutcome: The request handler will be able to parse incoming JSON webhook data into a usable JavaScript object.
successCriteria: JSON.parse() is used to convert the rawBody string into a JavaScript object inside the try block.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully implemented JSON parsing for the webhook payload.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure to parse the rawBody variable using JSON.parse() inside the try block.
steps.feedbackWrong: The parsing logic is missing or incorrect. Use JSON.parse() on the rawBody string to convert it to a JavaScript object.

steps.title: Extract signature from headers
steps.instruction: Inside the handleRequest function, after parsing the JSON payload, extract the webhook signature from the request headers. The signature is typically in a header like 'x-webhook-signature' or 'x-signature'.
steps.hint: You can access request headers using req.headers. Look for a header that contains the signature, such as 'x-webhook-signature'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Extracting a specific header value
const signature = req.headers['x-webhook-signature'];
steps.expectedOutcome: The code will extract the signature from the request headers, preparing it for verification in the next step.
successCriteria: The signature is extracted from the request headers and stored in a variable.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully extracted the signature from the headers. This is a crucial step for verifying the webhook's authenticity.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're extracting the signature from the correct header (e.g., 'x-webhook-signature').
steps.feedbackWrong: The signature extraction seems incorrect. Remember to access the header from req.headers and assign it to a variable.

steps.title: Verify webhook signature
steps.instruction: Inside the try block of handleRequest, call your verifySignature function with the extracted signature and rawBody, then check if the verification passes.
steps.hint: Call verifySignature(signature, rawBody) and store the result in a variable. Use an if statement to handle the verification outcome.
steps.expectedOutcome: The signature verification is performed after extracting the signature and parsing the payload, with conditional logic to handle the result.
successCriteria: verifySignature is called with the signature and rawBody, and an if statement checks the result.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully implemented the signature verification step, ensuring only authenticated webhook requests are processed.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you call verifySignature with both the signature and rawBody, then check the result with an if statement.
steps.feedbackWrong: The signature verification step is missing or incorrect. You need to call verifySignature and handle the validation outcome.

steps.title: Handle verification results
steps.instruction: Inside the handleRequest function, after the signature verification, add conditional logic to send appropriate responses: if verified, respond with 200 OK and the payload; if not verified, respond with 401 Unauthorized.
steps.hint: Use an if-else statement to check the verification result and call res.writeHead() with the appropriate status code and content-type header, then res.end() with a JSON response.
steps.expectedOutcome: The webhook receiver now responds with appropriate HTTP status codes and JSON messages based on whether the signature verification passes or fails.
successCriteria: The handleRequest function contains an if-else statement that sends a 200 response for verified signatures and a 401 response for unverified signatures.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! Your webhook receiver now properly handles verification results with appropriate HTTP responses.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some response logic, but make sure you have both success (200) and failure (401) cases with proper JSON responses.
steps.feedbackWrong: The verification result handling is missing or incorrect. Add conditional logic to respond with 200 OK for verified signatures and 401 Unauthorized for unverified signatures.

steps.title: Start the HTTP server
steps.instruction: Inside the webhookReceiver function, create and start the HTTP server using the handleRequest function you defined earlier.
steps.hint: Use the http.createServer() method to create a server instance, then call its .listen() method with the port constant.
steps.expectedOutcome: The server will be created and ready to listen for incoming webhook requests.
successCriteria: An HTTP server is created using http.createServer() with handleRequest, and it listens on the specified port.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created and started the HTTP server. Your webhook receiver is now ready to accept requests.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're using http.createServer() with the handleRequest function and calling .listen() with the port.
steps.feedbackWrong: The server isn't properly started. Check that you're creating the server with http.createServer(handleRequest) and calling .listen() with the port constant.

steps.title: Add error handling and logging
steps.instruction: Inside the handleRequest function, add a console.log statement to log successful signature verification and enhance the existing catch block to log errors.
steps.hint: Add console.log('Signature verified successfully') after successful verification and console.error('Error:', error.message) in the catch block.
steps.expectedOutcome: The handleRequest function will include logging for both successful verification and error cases, making debugging easier.
successCriteria: The handleRequest function contains console.log for success and console.error for errors in the catch block.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added proper logging for both successful verification and error handling, making your webhook receiver production-ready.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added some logging, but make sure to include both success logging (console.log) and error logging (console.error) in the catch block.
steps.feedbackWrong: The handleRequest function doesn't include the required logging statements. Add console.log for successful verification and console.error for errors.
